ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-signing screening of every shareholder, UBO, gérant and authorized signatory against the French Fonds de Terrorisme (FTO) freezing list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and UN Consolidated List, supplemented by OFAC SDN screening for USD-rail and U.S. nexus risk. PEP status is verified using commercial databases and must be recorded for enhanced due diligence under Article L. 561-10 CMF. The business profile (no-code website builder; SaaS billing via Stripe/Paddle) is assessed as Low Risk Standard, but all CDD records must be retained for five years post-relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises (available at guichet-entreprises.fr); name availability cross-checked through the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and Infogreffe.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The dénomination sociale must be written in Latin characters; foreign-script names are accepted only in Latin transliteration. The name must contain a distinctive element and may not mislead as to the corporate form, public-sector status or regulated activity; it must comply with ordre public and lawful business morality. For a SARL, the name need not include 'SARL', but if the company name does not include a corporate-form suffix/prefix, the form must be clearly stated in the articles of association and on commercial documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / banquier / Banque de France (requires credit institution license or prior ministerial authorization)
Assurance / assureur (requires regulatory approval or insurance licensee status)
Mutuelle / mutuel (reserved for mutual insurers with ACPR approval)
État / République / Préfecture / Ministère / Commune / Défense Nationale (reserved or misleading public-law character)
Chambre de commerce et d'industrie / Chambre de métiers (reserved to public chambers)
Société de gestion / gestion de portefeuille (requires AMF authorization unless used only as descriptive phrase)
Fondation / Institut national / Université (requires statutory qualification or prior authorization)
Euro / franc (restricted by monetary rules and may be misleading if used in finance sector)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the INPI or the Guichet Unique registrar rejects the proposed name, the applicant may first file written observations through guichet-entreprises.fr. An administrative appeal (recours gracieux) may be lodged with the Director-General of INPI within two months from notification, citing the availability decision under Article R. 711-12 of the French Intellectual Property Code. If the refusal originates from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, the proposed gérant may apply to the presiding judge of the commercial court for an order directing registration (Code de commerce, Article L. 123-3). A fresh name reservation may be filed immediately with a revised distinctive element; there is no blocking stare decisis effect of a rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a SARL under Articles L. 123-11-2 and L. 123-11-3 of the French Commercial Code provided the domiciliation service provider holds the required declaration/agreement, the address is real, and the registered office is identified in the articles of association. For a low-code website builder (ISIC 6201) there is no industry-specific physical premises mandate; a virtual office may be used for administrative seat, but the company must be able to produce records and receive official service at that address. The domiciliation arrangement must be reported to the Companies Registry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Estimated annual unannounced-inspection probability for a low-risk ISIC 6201 SARL is approximately 2% in the absence of tax or AML flags; this rises to roughly 20-30% when a virtual office is used without a valid domiciliation agreement or if mismatches appear in UBO/address data during tax audit triage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); corporate taxpayer portal at impots.gouv.fr / professionnels.impots.gouv.fr; incorporation and tax registration performed through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; non-resident entities without a French permanent establishment register for VAT via the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) or through the European OSS portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of the SARL, the Guichet Unique transmits the filing to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and DGFiP, which automatically issue the SIREN (9 digits), SIRET (14 digits), NAF/APE code (6201Z) and the intra-Community VAT number (FR + 2-digit control key + SIREN). For a foreign entity without a French registered office, the applicant must file Form 3559-SD with the SIE/SIEE, provide evidence of foreign legal existence, foreign VAT registration if any, a French fiscal representative appointment where required, and a description of French taxable activities; the VAT number is normally issued within 15 to 30 days after verification, with effect from the commencement of taxable operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a French SARL is a capital company subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at the headline rate of 25%, with a 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit for companies with turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million; the territoriality principle applies, so only profits arising from French establishments or French operations are taxable, while foreign branch profits are normally exempt, and losses from foreign branches are not deductible.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box election. Available elections include: (i) option for a qualified family SARL (SARL de famille) to be taxed as a transparent partnership under Article 239 bis AA of the CGI; (ii) option for VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 256 C of the CGI; (iii) option for French fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A of the CGI for a French parent holding at least 95% of the subsidiary shares; (iv) option to pay VAT on actual receipts (taxes sur les encaissements) under Article 269 of the CGI; (v) no elective hybrid mismatch reversal is permitted, and the ATAD 2 anti-hybrid rules under Article 212 bis B of the CGI disallow double-deduction and deduction-without-inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 36,800 for services and EUR 91,900 for goods (franchise en base de TVA, Article 293 B of the CGI) for the preceding year, with tolerance limits of EUR 39,100 and EUR 101,000 respectively for the current year; for the low-code website builder digital services, a SARL is compulsorily registered for VAT from inception if taxable turnover is expected to exceed the franchise, and cross-border B2C digital sales to EU consumers are subject to mandatory VAT registration or OSS usage without a threshold once annual distance/OSS supplies exceed EUR 10,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing and e-reporting under the French e-invoicing reform (Article 289 of the CGI): applicable from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size companies and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs, including all SARLs; invoices must be issued in an interoperable structured format (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) and transmitted through the Public Invoicing Portal (PPF) or a certified Dematerialization Partner Platform (PDP) via API connection; France applies a centralized transmission and validation hub model (Y-type) rather than a real-time fiscal stamping or pre-clearance system, but every invoice metadata set must be transmitted to DGFiP and retained for a 6-year audit period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the European Union qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 262-I of the CGI provided the goods are physically exported and documentary proof is retained; offshore B2B services, including software hosting, platform access and digital development services consumed outside the EU, are outside the scope of French VAT under Article 259-1 of the CGI when the recipient is established outside the EU; intra-EU supplies of digital services to business customers are zero-rated where a valid intra-Community VAT number is provided and the reverse charge is applied; B2C digital services to EU consumers are taxable at the consumer's place of residence and are reported via the OSS regime; the 0% rate is available only for genuine exports substantiated by complete transport, customs and payment evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU - Document Administratif Unique, including the MRN customs clearance reference)
Commercial Invoice stating the 0% VAT export basis, incoterms, and description of the digital/software services or goods
Bill of Lading or CMR international waybill evidencing physical movement outside the EU
Continuous Transport Evidence or signed delivery proof from the overseas recipient
Customer's Intra-Community VAT Number validated in VIES for intra-EU zero-rated supplies
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 proof of foreign currency receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Article 1741 of the CGI, fraudulent export zero-rating, falsification of export documentation, or fictitious export declarations are criminal tax fraud punishable by a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and 5 years' imprisonment, increased to EUR 750,000 and 7 years for organized fraud or laundering; Article 1788 A of the CGI imposes a 40% deficiency penalty on the VAT amount improperly zero-rated or wrongfully credited, while Article 1758 A subjects missing export declarations to a 5%-10% administrative fine; the VAT advantage is retrospectively clawed back with a 5% monthly late-interest (intérêt de retard), and deliberate misstatements attract the 80% abuse-of-right penalty under Article 1729 of the CGI; the standard assessment window is 3 years, extended to 6 or 10 years in cases of hidden activity, aggressive tax arrangements, or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF); foreign exchange and monetary-payment policy in France is exercised jointly by the Banque de France, the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) within the French Ministry of the Economy, and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the prudential banking and payment-institution supervisor. There is no standalone foreign exchange administration in France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the euro. Under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, all restrictions on capital movements and payments between Member States and between Member States and third countries are prohibited. No exchange-control authorization or central-bank license is required for capital subscriptions, profit distributions, loan repayments, liquidation proceeds, royalty payments, or service payments. Current-account transactions, including invoices issued by the French SARL to non-residents, are freely payable in EUR or foreign currency. Capital-account transactions, including inbound share capital and outbound repayment of equity, are equally free of foreign-exchange approval. Profit remittance from the SARL is not blocked at the FX level, but practical hurdles exist: the annual accounts must be approved by the shareholders; the legal reserve must be constituted at 5% of profits until it reaches 10% of share capital; distributions are prohibited if net assets fall below share capital plus non-distributable reserves; and the paying bank must complete AML/KYC and source-of-funds checks under Articles L. 561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code. There is no obligatory prior tax clearance certificate, no ceiling on transfers, and no forced conversion requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no required conversion ratio for export receipts in France. Export and cross-border service proceeds may be retained in EUR or in a foreign-currency account maintained with a French or EU bank. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0%. The only applicable obligation is statistical reporting by banks to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes and compliance with EU sanctions and AML rules. For the target company, which is a no-code website builder selling software subscriptions through payment service providers such as Stripe Billing and Paddle, the treatment of cross-border service receipts is identical to that of merchandise exports: no FX surrender, no timeline, and no conversion requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for EEA-licensed electronic-money institutions and fintech challenger banks that hold an EMI or banking licence passported into France, such as Wise Europe, Revolut Bank UAB, Qonto, or Shine. Low for offshore third-country digital EMIs. Legal constraints: under the EU Revised Payment Services Directive (EU) 2015/2366 and the French Monetary and Financial Code, only an ACPR-authorized or passported EEA payment institution may provide payment accounts and issue e-money to a French-resident legal entity. An offshore EMI without French passporting rights cannot lawfully hold the French SARL's treasury, and a bank or regulator may block or close such accounts. EMIs generally do not provide deposit-guarantee protection, cannot grant credit, and are unsuitable as a statutory blocked account for share-capital escrow. They are acceptable as an ancillary collection vehicle for subscription revenues if their underlying partner bank is an EEA credit institution, but the SARL should maintain its primary treasury and capital accounts with a fully licensed French or EU bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no French statutory rule requiring every director or shareholder of a SARL to appear physically before a bank. Remote opening is legally possible where the bank operates an ACPR-compliant video-identification procedure and applies the statutory AML/KYC interview. In practice, tier-one high-street banks generally require at least one physical appearance by the SARL manager or an authorized representative with signing authority for the initial corporate onboarding, particularly when the shareholder is non-resident. Online regulated fintech banks allow full remote onboarding using passport capture, video call, and e-signature. The safest and most efficient route for a non-resident-owned French SARL is to use a fully remote-capable regulated bank and, if the transaction involves a large capital escrow or commercial-lending relationship, to prepare for an in-person interview at a Paris or Lyon branch. Apostilled powers of attorney are required if a local representative will open the account on behalf of the foreign director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: French corporate with a 100% non-resident shareholder, no physical operating office, and a registered-office contract instead of a lease; bank underwriting flags a possible shell company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract; signed SARL statutes; certificate of incorporation; registered-office arrangement (contrat de domiciliation) with the domiciliation agent; beneficial-ownership declaration; personal identification and residence proof of the shareholder and manager; business plan for the no-code website-builder activity; evidence of actual platform or customer base; bank statements or payment-processor dashboard reports from Stripe or Paddle; board/shareholder minutes; tax compliance letters or French tax declaration if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial share capital is a foreign personal account with a large lump-sum transfer, a crypto-asset liquidation, or an unexplained third-party payment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of personal bank statements; source-of-wealth statement; crypto-to-fiat exchange reports and transaction/chain-analysis reports where applicable; notarized sale deeds or inheritance documents; salary slips and tax declarations; contract evidencing the transfer; a declaration signed by the shareholder confirming the capital contribution; confirmation that no third-party reimbursement or nominee structure exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, PEP status, or a sanctions-list hit against the ultimate beneficial owner, a shareholder, or an anticipated counterparty in the payment chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official identity documents; PEP self-declaration; sanctions-screening results from the bank's system; an external legal opinion or compliance memorandum; curriculum vitae and professional references; a written explanation of the alleged media item; source-of-wealth report prepared by a French accountant or notary; confirmation of tax residence and tax identification numbers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payment rails are only foreign PSPs (Stripe Billing and Paddle), with large inbound subscription flows from non-EU customers and no immediately visible high-value contracts or inventory; the bank asks for evidence that the SARL is a genuine operating company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company website and software platform URL; applicant and customer contracts; terms and privacy policies; payment-processor merchant records and settlement reports; infrastructure invoices for hosting and software services; trademark registration if any; COC or other seller identifiers in Paddle; a list of target markets; projected cash-flow model; accounting package excerpts or invoices for operational expenditure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For initial share capital before SARL registration, route the contribution from the non-resident shareholder via SWIFT MT103 if outside the EEA, or via SEPA Credit Transfer if the contributor bank is in the EEA, to the French bank account opened in the name of the société en formation, i.e., the 'SARL en constitution', clearly marked as blocked share capital. The beneficiary bank will issue the legal certificate of deposit. The remittance instruction should state 'APPORTS EN NUMÉRAIRE / CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION / SARL EN FORMATION'. For balance-of-payments statistical classification, the transaction must be classified by the bank as a direct investment capital contribution from a non-resident to a resident French corporate; where the bank's interface requires a purpose code or BOP statistical category, select the direct-investment/equity-participation code in the Banque de France reporting menu, not a service, loan, or income category. If the contribution is in foreign currency, the receiving bank converts at market spot; no exchange-control approval is needed. The contribution must remain blocked until the Tribunal de Commerce registers the SARL. After registration, the account is released as the operating account. For a capital increase after registration, the same routing is used, labelled 'AUGMENTATION DE CAPITAL', and the bank will require a shareholder resolution, updated articles of association or a notarial deed, Kbis, and updated beneficial-ownership register. Verification deliverables include source-of-funds documentation, identity of each contributing shareholder, breakdown of share subscriptions, and the registered deed or certificate provided by the legal representative.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EEA payments to suppliers, contractors, and subscription vendors, use SEPA Credit Transfer, an instant SEPA Credit Transfer where urgency requires, or the TARGET2 settling system for high-value EUR interbank payments. The instruction should be prepared as ISO 20022 XML with beneficiary IBAN and BIC and the underlying invoice or purchase-order reference in the remittance information. For non-EEA disbursements, use SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary bank's SWIFT BIC, the beneficiary account in the relevant local or IBAN format, and a precise narrative such as 'SERVICE FEE / INVOICE NO. X / CONTRACT REFERENCE Y'; where the beneficiary bank must be funded separately, an MT202 COV cover payment is used. Settlement of trade and service debts should never be made through cash, unregistered virtual-currency transfers, or shell payment intermediaries unless the intermediary is a regulated financial institution. Commercial letters of credit are legally permissible under French law but are generally inefficient for a no-code software business; if required by a supplier for physical infrastructure or procurement, issue an irrevocable documentary letter of credit under UCP600, in EUR, payable at sight, with confirmation from a European bank. All outbound disbursements are subject to sanctions screening, AML review, and the bank's account-usage monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts (FX outright forwards) in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other convertible currency pairs, available under an ISDA Master Agreement or the bank's standard corporate treasury terms, limited to the entity's actual forecast foreign-currency exposure from subscription revenue and supplier contracts.

Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) for currencies that do not have a fully deliverable market or where the SARL does not hold a local settlement account; permitted as hedging instruments with an ACPR-authorized counterparty, with the calculation in EUR and settlement in EUR, subject to documented underlying exposure.

Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for longer-term balance-sheet hedging of material non-EUR debt or intercompany capital flows, subject to EMIR clearing, margining, and ISDA documentation, and appropriate for the SARL only where exposure exceeds the threshold at which plain forwards are operationally less efficient.

FX swaps (swap de devises) for rolling short-term liquidity conversion between EUR and a transitory non-EUR treasury position, concluded on the same credit documentation and permissioned solely for treasury-liquidity mismatches, not for speculative trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SARL shareholders; filed subsequently with the commercial court registry through the INPI one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction may be issued; failure to file approved accounts may result in a fine of approximately EUR 1,500, increased to approximately EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance. France has no automatic strike-off solely for missing one filing, but prolonged inactivity or repeated non-compliance may lead to judicial or administrative removal procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the INPI formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after approval of the accounts, or within 2 months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a court injunction, civil and administrative enforcement, and fines of approximately EUR 1,500 or EUR 3,000 for repeat violations. No fixed annual franchise tax or automatic annual strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and financial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronically by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company, subject to the applicable tax-calendar extension rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest of 0.20% per month, and potential additional penalties for materially incorrect or omitted information. Tax enforcement does not ordinarily cause immediate corporate strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return or annual VAT summary where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: According to the company's VAT regime; annual CA12 filing generally follows the applicable VAT-year deadline, while companies under the normal regime file periodic CA3 returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted VAT filings may trigger a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest, estimated assessment, recovery measures, and penalties for inaccurate reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI beneficial ownership register through the statutory formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual filing is required where previously filed information remains correct; changes must generally be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare or update beneficial ownership information may result in formal notice, criminal fines for the legal representative, restrictions on filing services, and possible judicial enforcement. It does not create an automatic annual strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for a SARL when it exceeds at least 2 of the following 3 thresholds at the relevant statutory test date: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional group-company tests may apply to parent or controlled companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Plan Comptable Général. IFRS is generally not used for standalone SARL statutory accounts and is principally relevant to qualifying consolidated groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual beneficial-owner confirmation when the recorded information remains accurate. The SARL should conduct an annual internal confirmation of shareholders, voting rights, control arrangements, managers, and beneficial owners. Any change in ownership, control, management, or beneficial-owner status must be reflected in corporate records and reported to the INPI register generally within 30 days. Share transfers must also be recorded and supported by the required transfer documentation and amended shareholder information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register or equivalent corporate record of shareholders, shareholdings, and share transfers
Register of shareholders' decisions and annual accounts approval decisions
Register or minute book of management and shareholder proceedings
Current corporate records identifying the SARL managers and their appointment, removal, and powers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 325-1,625 per year for a standard registered-office and corporate secretarial service; France generally does not require a separate registered agent in the common-law sense
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,200-6,500 for a small SARL subject to statutory audit; complex or group-company audits may exceed USD 10,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,701 of taxable profit for small enterprises meeting the CGI Article 219-I-b SME conditions; research tax credit (CIR) at up to 30% of eligible R&D expenditure; SME innovation tax credit (CII); young innovative company (JEI) exemptions under certain labour and ownership conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime_note: French law permits indefinite carryforward of fiscal losses under CGI Article 209-I, but each year the offset is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000. Loss carryback is limited to one fiscal year and EUR 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CERFA form 2065-SD and annexed liasse fiscale (2050-SD to 2059-SD); mandatory electronic filing through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal using EFID/GEIS or an EDI partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual definitive result declaration; quarterly instalments (acomptes) due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; final balance due with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: the second working day after 1 May of the following year. For any other fiscal year-end: within three months of the close of the financial year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD front page — 'Entreprise désignée / SIREN / SIRET / APE / régime fiscal'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the SARL, its legal form, registered office, principal no-code website-builder activity, tax registration number and applicable corporate income tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers operating through a French permanent establishment must identify the French branch and, where required, appoint and disclose a French tax representative under Article 1649-bis B of the CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: States the final taxable profit after deducting deductible operating expenses, depreciation, amortisation, provisions and tax losses carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with a French PE must include only the PE's French-source trading profit; head-office charges and intercompany payments are deductible only to the extent they satisfy the arm's length standard and are substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2051-SD — 'Passage du résultat comptable au résultat fiscal' (réintégrations and déductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciles accounting profit to taxable profit by adding back disallowed expenses and applying temporary or permanent deductions such as tax credits and accelerated depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back thin-capitalisation interest exceeding Article 212 limits and transfer-pricing adjustments under Article 57 where payments are made to non-resident related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details the opening fiscal loss balance, losses set off in the current year and the remaining balance that may be carried forward as permitted by CGI Article 209-I.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French PE of a foreign corporation may carry forward French tax losses only against future French PE profits subject to the anti-loss-trafficking restrictions in Article 209-III.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Lists eligible tax credits such as the research tax credit, foreign tax credits and innovation tax credits claimed against the current corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a treaty gives foreign tax relief, attach the relevant treaty-relief certificate, Form 2067-SD or foreign Tax Residency Certificate before the tax credit is accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD — Computation of total IS due after quarterly instalments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shows corporate income tax due for the year, deducts quarterly instalments already paid, applies available credits and produces the final balance payable with the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same filing must disclose any distribution of profits, the corresponding non-resident dividend withholding tax and the treaty basis for a reduced rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a late-payment surcharge of 10% if the tax is not paid within 30 days, increasing to 40% after formal assessment notice and to 80% in cases of bad faith or fraud; monthly late-payment interest of 0.40% (4.8% per annum) accrues from the original due date. Additional fixed fines (currently EUR 150–500) apply for incomplete transfer-pricing or documentation filings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for non-resident corporate shareholders; 12.8% for non-resident individuals not fiscally domiciled in France. Qualifying EU parent companies may benefit from a 0% rate under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive after satisfying the holding-period and anti-abuse tests.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must deliver a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by its state of tax residence, together with a beneficial-ownership statement and, where applicable, evidence of shareholding and holding period. The French paying agent applies the treaty-reduced rate only if such documentation is provided before payment; otherwise the statutory French WHT is applied and the excess may be recovered by filing a reimbursement claim with the DGFIP within the statutory limitation deadline.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic law generally imposes 0% withholding tax on interest paid to non-resident creditors, unless the creditor is resident in a non-cooperative State or an abusive scheme exists. Royalties paid to non-resident companies for IP, trademarks or know-how are subject to a statutory withholding rate of 33.33%, reduced to 0%–10% under most French income tax treaties where the beneficial ownership requirement is met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory French Local File and Master File documentation applies when the consolidated annual net turnover of the French entity or group reaches EUR 400,000,000. A simplified transfer-pricing declaration in the annual return is required for smaller entities only when the French revenue or intercompany transaction volume triggers Article L.13-AA/L.13-AB thresholds; all cross-border controlled transactions must nevertheless respect the arm's length principle under CGI Article 57.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies a substance-over-form analysis and an abusive-tax-scheme doctrine through Article L.64 of the French Tax Procedures Code. A French SARL engaged in no-code website building must demonstrate real local business substance — premises, employees, management decisions, active client contracts and bank flows — otherwise it may be recharacterised as an artificial shell company and its treaty or EU Directive benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Wilful Under-declaration of Digital Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording zero or artificially low revenue from website-builder sales handled through Stripe, Paddle or a foreign merchant of record, while routing subscription proceeds to an offshore account without declaring them to the French tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 80% tax penalty for bad faith or fraudulent concealment, late-payment interest at 0.40% monthly, full reassessment of corporate income tax, and criminal prosecution under CGII Article 1741 carrying up to EUR 250,000 fine and 7 years imprisonment, with higher aggravating penalties for organised fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or instigate false returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax liabilities and penalties; courts may impose personal bankruptcy measures, bar the director from managing a French company, order asset confiscation and travel bans, and impose imprisonment.
